This is a fundamental result in metric geometry, and it has numerous applications in various fields, including analysis, geometry, and topology.

The proof of this statement involves showing that if (M, d) is complete, then any sequence (F_n) of nonempty closed subsets of M with the given properties has a nonempty intersection. Conversely, if (M, d) is not complete, then there exists a sequence (F_n) of nonempty closed subsets of M with the given properties that has no nonempty intersection.

The statement also highlights the importance of the diameter of a set in metric geometry. The condition - F_{n+1} ⊂ F_n - diam F_n → 0 as n → ∞ ensures that the sets F_n are "shrinking" in some sense, which is necessary for the existence of a nonempty intersection.

Overall, this result has far-reaching implications for our understanding of metric spaces and their properties.
